findings.issue: Every checked operation allocates its 17-byte message even when it cannot fail (three unused allocations in a row), and the revert copies it with a word loop, so 'revert with "MATH_ADD_OVERFLOW"' takes about 15 lines.
findings.rule: Drop allocations whose memory is never read on the path; a string literal stored at a fresh pointer and copied into an Error(string) buffer is 'revert with <literal>'.

notes: solc 0.4.24 Aragon app. No explicit loop in Lido.sol or in the libraries it uses (StakeLimitUtils, UnstructuredStorage, SafeMath variants). The 10 whiles are implicit word-wise memory copies (revert strings, getEVMScriptExecutor/canPerform returns, eip712Domain's strings, initialize), counted as P7. Storage is unstructured: packed slots are read through '>> 128' and uint128() (P15). The division-by-zero guard of getSharesByPooledEth prints as 'assert <total pooled ether>', which is the 0.4 invalid-opcode behaviour, faithful. No semantic error found.
summary: Faithful, loop-free text; readable except where the branchless min/max of the stake limit is distributed into very long expressions and where SafeMath string messages are allocated and copied word by word.
